description: AETHER-G (Autonomous Edge Thermal & Hazard Emergency Responder powered by Gemma) is tackling Flame in Freefall with an edge-deployable fire safety copilot using local open-weights AI (Gemma). Operating completely offline for deep-space reliability, our tool analyzes microgravity combustion data (Saffire/BASS) to detect smoldering anomalies and advise crew in real time. Seeking ML/Python devs, UI/UX designers, and aerospace/physics thinkers!
summary: In microgravity, fire doesn't rise and smoke doesn't go up — so ceiling smoke detectors miss smoldering cables while floating dust triggers false alarms. On deep-space missions, a radio round-trip can take up to 24 minutes, so crews can't wait for Earth. AETHER-G is an offline Edge AI fire-safety copilot powered by local Google Gemma: a two-stage pipeline fuses multi-gas (CO, CO2, VOC, CH4), particulate, airflow, thermocouple and infrared thermal data to detect smoldering minutes before flame, reject dust false alarms, and give the crew grounded, spoken mitigation steps — with no cloud and no internet. Built on real NASA Saffire I-VI and BASS/BASS-II microgravity fire data from the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics portal, with a live backend, a crew dashboard, and a NASA telemetry replay mode.
details:
THE PROBLEM

In microgravity there is no buoyancy-driven convection: flames are spherical, smoke does not rise to ceiling detectors, and smoldering cable insulation can release toxic CO for hours before any visible flame. Floating cabin dust fools smoke-only detectors. On Artemis and Mars missions, up to 24 minutes of one-way radio delay means the crew cannot call Earth for help.

THE SOLUTION

AETHER-G is an offline Edge AI fire-safety copilot powered by Google Gemma 4 e4b running 100% on-device. A two-stage pipeline: (1) a fast rule-based Stage-1 detector fuses CO/CO2, VOC, CH4, PM2.5, airflow, three thermocouples and a 32x24 infrared thermal frame — CO above 25 ppm while rising latches SMOLDERING_ANOMALY; a dust event (PM spike with flat CO and temperature) is rejected and stays NOMINAL; (2) a local Gemma 4 model (via oMLX, temperature 0.0) with retrieval over real NASA Saffire/BASS facts gives the crew three grounded mitigation steps and voice output. Everything runs air-gapped — no cloud, no internet.

WHAT WE BUILT (working, live)

- Public repo: https://github.com/edo26/aether-g (MIT) — telemetry simulator (nominal / dust / smoldering / airgapped scenarios), FastAPI backend with Stage-1 detector and Gemma/RAG advisor, feed tool, ESP32 firmware skeleton.

- Live backend: https://aether-be.fakhrads.dev (health, ingest, thermal, status, advisories, chat endpoints).

- Live crew dashboard: https://aether-g.fakhrads.dev — stage-1 status, 8 live sensor trends, 32x24 thermal heatmap, Gemma crew advisories, Saffire/BASS detector evidence, Live backend / Captured replay source switch.

- Local RAG knowledge base in the repo (data/rag/psi_fire_safety_brief.md) extracted from NASA PSI: Saffire I-III, BASS, BASS-II, SAME/SAME-R and DAFT investigations, including real Saffire-I telemetry channels (pressure, temperature, smoke detector, radiometer, anemometer).

NASA DATA USED

NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI): Saffire I-VI and BASS/BASS-II microgravity combustion investigations (see NASA Data links). The detector's thresholds and the RAG facts are grounded in these experiments; the demo telemetry is synthetic fixtures modelled on them, and the dashboard labels replay data as such.

TEAM

Anggy Edo Prasetya (initiator, frontend/dashboard, pitch), Fakhri Adi Saputra (backend, Edge AI, detector, RAG), Heri Cahyono (hardware, ESP32, sensors).
